title: Uddhava in Vraja
hookLine: a learned friend arrives in Vraja at sunset, and a father asks him one question all night
carry: loving God like your own child
tomorrow: why would Krishna run from a fight?

lines: NANDA MEETS HIM AT THE DOOR.
cards: In Mathura, Krishna calls his friend and counselor Uddhava aside. Go to Vraja, he tells him. Comfort my father and mother.
Comfort the gopis. Tell them what I've told you. So Uddhava drives out to the village Krishna grew up in, and arrives at sunset.
The cows are coming home, raising dust. Calves are calling. There's the sound of milking, lamps being lit, butter being churned.
An ordinary evening in a place that has been missing someone for a long time. The first to meet him is Nanda, Krishna's foster father.

teach.b: Nanda embraces Uddhava as if he were Krishna himself, washes his feet, feeds him, and sits him down. Then the questions, in paraphrase. Is he well?
Does Krishna remember us? Will he come back, even once, so we can see his face?
Nanda starts remembering out loud: the forest fire, the serpent in the river, the storm. He can't finish. His voice breaks.
Beside him, Yashoda listens to every word, and the text says her tears won't stop. Uddhava answers as a learned man would. You two are truly fortunate, he says, to love him like this.
Then he says something large. Krishna isn't only your son. He has no mother or father of his own, no one who is his and no one who isn't.

teach.h: HE IS THE SELF OF ALL.
teach.b: He is within everyone, the Self of all beings. Will that help a mother whose tears won't stop? The Bhagavata doesn't pretend it does.
It lets them talk through the whole night.

teach.h: VATSALYA: LOVING GOD AS YOUR CHILD.
teach.b: Vaishnava teachers have a name for Nanda and Yashoda's love: vatsalya, loving God the way a parent loves a child.
The big truth, he's in everyone, sits right beside the small grief, does he remember us, and the learned man calls the grieving parents fortunate. Then morning comes.

teach.h: AT DAWN, THEY CHURN AND SING.
teach.b: The women of Vraja are up churning butter, singing about Krishna as they churn, and the song carries over the village.
It's why many Hindu homes keep a small baby Krishna who is bathed, dressed and fed each morning: God, loved as your own child.

how: In Vaishnava traditions, the chapters of Uddhava's visit to Vraja are read aloud in Bhagavata recitations and sung in devotional songs, Nanda and Yashoda are honored as models of vatsalya, parental love for Krishna, and many families keep a small image of baby Krishna, often called Bal Gopal or Laddu Gopal, bathed, dressed and fed each morning.

o: Krishna's elder brother, who stayed behind in Vraja
the cowherd chief who raised Krishna as his son
Krishna's friend, sent to comfort the family he left

games.q: Uddhava in Vraja — tap the pairs.
p: he is the Self of all beings

s: Krishna sends Uddhava to comfort his parents and the gopis
he asks his friend to go to Vraja and tell them his message.
Uddhava tells Nanda that Krishna belongs to his family alone
he says Krishna has no mother or father of his own: he is within everyone.
the Bhagavata says Uddhava's teaching ends Nanda's grief at once
it doesn't settle anything quickly: they talk through the whole night.

games.q: your cousin says loving baby Krishna is for beginners: real devotion is knowing God is in everyone. by today's story, what fits?
o: agree. once you know the big truth, the baby stories can go.
both. Uddhava says he's the Self of all, and still calls Yashoda's love fortunate.
disagree. the Bhagavata never says God is in everyone.
games.why: in 10.46 Uddhava teaches that Krishna is the Self of all beings, and calls Nanda and Yashoda fortunate for loving him as their son. the text keeps both.

practice: Let the body be heavy on the chair and picture Krishna as Yashoda knew him: a small child, butter on his hands.
If you pray, offer him something small in your mind, a little butter or a sweet, the way many families do each morning, with a parent's tenderness.
If you don't, bring to mind a household that is missing someone and just sit in that house for a minute, the way Uddhava sat with Nanda, listening.

wordCard.voice: Uddhava, Krishna's trusted friend and counselor, sent to comfort the family he left behind. Today, a father who asks if he's remembered, and a love Vaishnavas call vatsalya.

carryVoice: Your line: loving God like your own child. Vatsalya, Yashoda's love, which the learned Uddhava called fortunate. See you tomorrow.

sources.ref: Bhagavata Purana 10.46 (Uddhava sent to Vraja; his night with Nanda and Yashoda; the dawn churning)
